edge_cases_and_observations.observation: verify_log detects entry.get('signature') is None → marks as tampered.
verify_log correctly detects tampered entry because signature no longer matches mutated canonical JSON.
verify_log detects missing signature field → marks as tampered.
log_event raises ValueError — callers must use recognized event types.
log_event raises ValueError listing missing fields — callers cannot silently produce incomplete entries.
_append_to_file catches OSError silently — entry still held in-memory and returned. Best-effort persistence.

At audit.py line 189, entry.update(fields) allows a caller to inject a 'timestamp' key that replaces the auto-generated ISO 8601 timestamp from line 187. Current test fixtures pass 'timestamp': 'test_timestamp_value' which overrides the real timestamp. Recommendation: reject or ignore caller-supplied 'timestamp', 'log_id', 'event_type', and 'signature' keys to prevent timestamp spoofing and maintain audit integrity. Not a spec violation in v1, but a hardening gap for production.

Default key 'default-key' (line 38) is weak and predictable. v_spec.md mandates 'default-key' as the default, so this is spec-compliant, but production deployment MUST override AUDIT_HMAC_KEY with a strong, randomly generated key.

The HMAC key is fixed per process lifetime. No built-in key rotation means key compromise invalidates all signatures. Future enhancement: support key versioning or key rotation without breaking existing signatures.

_init_rotation() runs at module import time (line 236). In long-running processes (e.g., production gunicorn), rotation only triggers when a new worker starts. The spec states 'renamed at midnight' as design intent; a cron-based or time-based rotation trigger would be needed for production use.
